#2147. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

#2146. Chelsea news: three positives and two disappointments... verdict on five players sent to Strasbourg

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 07:02

Very active in the last summer transfer window, Strasbourg signed five players from Chelsea. A few weeks after their arrival in Alsace, what is the verdict on their first steps with the club?

Revived by a home thrashing of Auxerre (5-1) after four consecutive defeats, Strasbourg have had a stop-start opening to the season.

Probably not helped by too big a squad overhaul in the last summer window, with close to £85m (€100m) spent and 17 signings registered, the Alsace club are suffering the full effect of a transfer mistake recently highlighted by Ismael Doukoure: a sizeable quota of foreign players and not a single signing with any Ligue 1 experience.

Among the summer arrivals, Hugo Oliveira’s side signed five players from Chelsea, the club with which Strasbourg share the same owner, BlueCo, in a collaboration designed to make transactions between the two sides easier.

They are Brazilian forward Deivid Washington, who cost £13.6m (€16m), English attacking midfielder Omari Kellyman, who cost £5.1m (€6m), Danish goalkeeper Filip Jorgensen on loan, Portuguese defensive midfielder Dario Essugo on loan and Swedish right-back Genesis Antwi on loan. Five players with radically different playing time and performances since the start of the 2026-27 season.

A few months after their arrival in France, what verdict can be drawn? Three positives and two disappointments stand out.

On the positive side, Dario Essugo has made four starts in seven appearances, with two goals and one assist. In terms of presence on the pitch, Filip Jorgensen outstrips the competition with nine starts in nine matches and a status strengthened by wearing the captain’s armband in three games. Although he has not yet kept a clean sheet, he has made 32 saves.

Genesis Antwi, for his part, has started eight times, with Hugo Oliveira only leaving him on the bench against Auxerre. The 19-year-old has just been rewarded for his good performances with a first call-up to Graham Potter’s Sweden squad for the upcoming international break and the Nations League matches against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Poland.

For the two other Chelsea recruits, however, the verdict is not very impressive. Deivid Washington, Strasbourg’s second most expensive signing of summer 2026, has so far been a flop: the Brazilian has still not played a single minute.

Finally, Omari Kellyman has only one appearance, for just six minutes, in a 3-0 defeat to Rennes on 25 October. In other words, the pile-up of players in Strasbourg’s squad has not stopped some from standing out while others remain on the sidelines. It is one way of weighing up the pros and cons of the club’s huge summer 2026 recruitment drive.

#2145. Who says Martin O'Neill is out of touch? Besiktas win was a tactical masterclass

The AGM that Celtic will hold at Parkhead on Tuesday, December 1, promises to be as explosive as any of the fireworks displays that were staged in the East End of Glasgow last night.

The Scottish champions’ performance in their home Europa League league phase match against Besiktas last night was, after a few damp squib displays in recent weeks, pretty incendiary too.

As rockets lit up the night air around the stadium and the sound of pyrotechnics being set off rang out, Martin O’Neill’s men finally found their sparkle.

Beating opponents who were sitting in the automatic qualification spots in the table alongside the likes of Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen and Juventus and avoiding an unwanted record was always going to be a big ask.

But O’Neill, the septuagenarian whose suitability for his high-pressure, high-profile role has been widely questioned in the wake of losses to Rangers, Ferencvaros, Celta Vigo and Falkirk, showed the flame still burns brightly.

The Northern Irishman, who selected Sebastien Tounekti, Kasper Hogh and James Forrest in his front three, vowed that his men would go for it when he spoke to BBC Radio Scotland ahead of the game.

However, the flat first-half display looked a little like a damage-limitation exercise, an attempt by a manager who knew his side was lacking in confidence after winning just three of their previous 10 outings to avoid a heavy home reverse and further opprobrium from the stands.

That was understandable to an extent. The visitors, who had beaten Hoffenheim and Marseille and drawn with Crystal Palace in their opening three fixtures, had Leandro Trossard, the Belgium international, pulling the strings for them in the middle of the park.

Still, an arena which is normally a cauldron of noise on big European nights and which is renowned across the world for its febrile atmosphere was eerily silent at times as the hosts sat back, concentrated on containing their rivals and offered next to nothing going forward.

Celtic left back Kieran Tierney at Parkhead last night (Image: Andrew Milligan)

Oh Hyeon-gyu, the South Korean international who spent a season-and-a-half at Celtic between 2022 and 2024 and won five major honours in that time, has clearly endeared himself to Besiktas supporters since moving to Istanbul in a €14m transfer in February.

The 25-year-old was given a huge ovation by the thousands of travelling supporters who had been shoehorned into the corner between the South Stand and the Lisbon Lions Stand when he emerged from the tunnel before kick-off.

He stood on the turf he once graced on a weekly basis in his bare feet and conducted a rendition of the “Oh Oh Song” which Black and Whites fans chant whenever he nets a goal. Eat your heart out Graham Roberts.

Oh is one of those players, and there have been quite a few of them over the years, who goes from strength to strength after departing Celtic. The 6ft 2in striker would have improved the hosts’ forward line in the first half last night.

Benjamin Nygren had the perfect chance to put the home team ahead and set proceedings alight in the seventh minute when he received the ball from Sebastien Tounekti in space in the opposition area. The Swede had time to control the pass and place his shot. He fired over the crossbar.

It was the only attempt on goal in the opening 45 minutes.

Vaclav Cerny, the former Rangers winger who returned to Parkhead for the first time since he sprayed Celtic fans with a water bottle after a 3-2 derby victory in March last year, was booed by the home support every time he got on the ball.

There was a huge roar in the first half when Liam Scales slid in and scythed the Czech down. There was precious little else for the green-and-white-clad hordes who had turned up – and thousands of green seats lay empty – to shout about.

Preferring the experience of Jordan Lotomba to the raw youthful exuberance of Colby Donovan was, regardless of the Swiss full-back’s lack of recent game time, a smart move.

The defender’s rustiness perhaps showed when he conceded a penalty with a rash foul on Ernest Poku. Junior Olaitan netted after Sam Johnstone had saved his initial effort.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill at Parkhead last night (Image: Andrew Milligan)

It was a cruel, even unfair, setback. Celtic had not looked like conceding up until that point. But O’Neill threw on Donovan, Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran for Lotomba, Tounekti and Forrest respectively. His inspired substitutions changed the game completely.

The 74-year-old has been portrayed as an old-school manager who is out of touch with the modern game in certain quarters in recent weeks as his charges have toiled and suffered painful losses. He silenced his doubters by producing a tactical masterclass.

Osmand equalised with his first touch of the ball and then set up Duran for a goal. The Colombian then put his side 3-2 ahead after Orkun Kokcu had lashed in a long-range effort from fully 30 yards out. That opportunist strike ultimately clinched a much-needed, morale-boosting and richly deserved victory.

“It was designed to do exactly what it did,” said O’Neill afterwards. “We have been playing Sunday, Thursday, Sunday, Thursday, Wednesday. We have played something like nine games in 24 days. Some players need a little breather. You can get re-energised from coming on the field.”

Can Celtic, who take on Kilmarnock in the William Hill Premiership at Parkhead on Sunday, tap into the feelgood factor this performance and result have generated and maintain this sort of form in the weeks ahead?

Their defensive play throughout the 90 minutes and the offensive play during the last half an hour augur well for the future.

Cameron Carter-Vickers, who was pilloried for his error-strewn showing against Falkirk last weekend, was a colossus before making way for Dane Murray due to hamstring tightness. Is there really friction between the centre-half and his manager? It didn’t look like it.

Celtic failed to push on after their 7-1 mauling of Hearts in the league last month - but this fine triumph over a formidable side indicates that better times might lie ahead.

#2144. It's Golden Bells! England star Jude Bellingham follows David Beckham into underwear modelling in steamy Calvin Klein photoshoot

Published: 11:57 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 11:58 EDT, 2 November 2026

First there was Golden Balls... now there's Golden Bells!

England midfielder Jude Bellingham is starring in an eye-catching underwear campaign for Calvin Klein - almost two decades after David Beckham signed a famous £20m deal to become the face of Emporio Armani.

Real Madrid star Bellingham, one of the stars of England's World Cup campaign, shot the campaign for the fashion giants in the Spanish capital.

The 23-year-old posed in a series of pictures wearing the Icon Cotton Stretch underwear - which retail at around £44 for a pack of three.

'I really enjoyed working on this campaign,' said Bellingham. 'I liked the idea of "the icon underneath" – that confidence starts with feeling comfortable in yourself.'

His underwear campaign follows on from that of fellow Real Madrid and England star Beckham - famously labelled Golden Balls by his wife Victoria.

Beckham signed a three-year deal with Emporio Armani in 2007, shortly after moving to LA Galaxy, with the company revealing sales went up 20 per cent once the news was announced.

Jude Bellingham models the Calvin Klein briefs in a series of images released today

'Calvin Klein is such an iconic brand, so it was great to bring that idea to life in my own way.'

David Beckham models Armani underwear in an advert seen at Macy's in San Francisco

Bellingham celebrated his 50th goal for Real Madrid with a strike against Racing Santander

Bellingham scored his 50th goal for Real on Sunday, in his fourth season at the club since joining from Borussia Dortmund.

The star, who began his career at Birmingham City, netted in a 3-0 win at Racing Santander.

Wearing the No5 shirt in which Zinedine Zidane made his name, Bellingham has now scored one more goal than the great Frenchman for Madrid — in 76 fewer matches.

It comes after he scored seven goals at the World Cup - setting a record for the number scored in one tournament by an England player. It included the final goal in the third-place playoff against France, which England won 6-4.

'Reaching 50 goals with Real Madrid is very special,' said Bellingham. 'Not only for me and my dreams but also for the team.'

'It’s very important for all players to score goals and make a difference in games.'

#2143. Barcelona: Raphinha to extend contract until 2030, three factors behind new deal

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 07:10

There could not be a better time for Raphinha to have his contract renewed by Barcelona. On Thursday, Barcelona will extend the deal of the Brazilian, who is the team’s current captain, until mid-2030, according to Trivela.

As well as being handed the captain’s armband this season, the Brazil international forward is arguably the best player in the world since the competitions began in August. Playing as a centre-forward, he has become a goal machine: 19 in only 13 matches in 2026-27.

It is a revolution the forward has experienced at the Catalan club since 2024. Signed in 2022, he was criticised and even questioned his future at the club, wavering over proposals from Saudi football.

The turning point came with the arrival of Hansi Flick, who convinced him to stay and turned him into one of the best players in the world, first on the left wing. In 2024-25, the German manager’s first year, he set career records for goals (34) and assists (22). After a poorer last year because of injuries, he has returned in full force this season.

His good form was one of the reasons for the renewal, as Trivela learned from an anonymous source who had contact with the negotiations. But it is not the only factor.

Raphinha and his staff understood that extending the contract was the best path given the moment he is experiencing and, in particular, because he is treated by the manager and the club as an important player. This is evident in every word Flick says about the Brazilian, always showering him with praise.

‘He is playing at a spectacular level. His strengths and characteristics fit our style perfectly. He always finds spaces to attack, and we also have players who can provide the final pass. He is very focused, he is our captain and he is showing his quality, which is important for us,’ Flick said after the 6-1 win over Alaves last weekend.

The captaincy mentioned by the manager was his own choice to reward the leadership of the number 11. Raphinha has always been a reference for younger players, which built trust in the dressing room, according to Trivela.

Having a foreigner as captain of one of the biggest clubs in the world is a weighty matter, but it came naturally. The Brazilian has won over the fans and created an identification that also made a difference in the renewal. For that reason there were no obstacles and the negotiation went smoothly for both sides.

When the new contract ends, Raphinha will be 33.

He is already the fourth Brazilian with the most goals for the club, with 94, level with Ronaldinho and behind only Neymar (105) and Rivaldo (130). In the overall ranking he is already in the top 25. In the Champions League, he has just equalled Robert Lewandowski, both with 23 goals, and is surpassed only by Luis Suarez and Lionel Messi.

He is a player who is increasingly becoming a Barcelona idol and, if he maintains his individual level and adds collective trophies, could finish the season as the best in the world.

#2142. Auxerre vs. Paris FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 05 Nov 2026 07:12, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 07:14

Ten places separate Auxerre and Paris FC in the Ligue 1 table ahead of Saturday's matchday 10 fixture at Stade de l'Abbe-Deschamps.

Liam Rosenior's men could theoretically finish the weekend joint-top if they secure maximum points against the side with the division's worst defensive record and Paris Saint-Germain lose to Troyes.

Rosenior faced considerable criticism after his forgettable spell at Chelsea earlier this year, but the Englishman has Paris FC flying after nine matchdays.

Les Bleus sit fourth in the division with 17 points from a possible 27, level with third-placed Lyon, one behind second-placed Lille and just three adrift of local rivals PSG.

Much of their early-season success admittedly stems from their strong form at Stade Jean-Bouin, where they remain unbeaten after collecting 13 of a possible 15 points.

However, they have struggled to replicate those performances on their travels, losing half of their four away matches, including the last two against Lorient (1-0) and Lens (2-1).

Paris have not won away since early October's 3-2 success at Marseille, and a return of just four points from 12 on the road undermines their prospects of drawing level with PSG before Luis Enrique's men face Troyes later on Saturday.

Will Still's Auxerre have made a patchy start to the campaign, compounded by their failure to keep clean sheets in eight of their nine Ligue 1 fixtures.

The 14th-placed club's only shutout came in September's 1-0 victory over Nice, but Les Ajaistes have been unable to keep opponents at bay since.

That defensive weakness leaves Still's team vulnerable, and they enter Saturday's encounter having conceded 23 league goals, three more than bottom-placed Le Havre, further underlining their difficulties.

While their 13 goals exceed the totals of all but two bottom-half clubs, Brest (16) and Strasbourg (17), this weekend's hosts leave themselves with considerable work to do by conceding far too freely.

Nonetheless, eagle-eyed observers will note that Auxerre have conceded just five goals in front of their supporters while scoring as many themselves, offering encouragement ahead of matchday 10.

Given Paris' away struggles, Les Ajaistes, who have collected seven points from 12 on home soil, will back themselves to secure maximum points against Rosenior's high-flying side.

Lamfia Dioubate was dismissed after 11 minutes of the 5-1 defeat to Strasbourg last time out, leaving Auxerre without the midfielder.

While Sekou Fofana is touch-and-go due to a groin issue, Bryan Okoh, Remy Labeau Lascary and Assane Diousse are all sidelined for the hosts.

Cameron Archer leads Auxerre's scoring charts with six goals, three more than Danny Namaso, and the Englishman will aim to build on his prolific start to the campaign.

Paris, meanwhile, could be without Ligue 1's leading scorer Lassine Sinayoko, whose eight goals surpass everyone else's tally in the competition, while his five assists underline his dual threat.

Given that Sinayoko has scored half of Les Bleus' 16 league goals, the visitors may have to rely on alternative sources; only Maxime Lopez and Pablo Pagis have also scored more than once for Rosenior's side, leaving the manager short of proven match-winners.

Apart from Sinayoko, the capital club have several other injury doubts: Adama Camara (hamstring), Luca Koleosho (muscle), Jonathan Ikone (thigh) and Nhoa Sangui (muscle) could all miss out.

Nardi; Makosso, Tuanzebe, Akpa; Sy, Danois, Ahamada, Oppegard; Faivre, Namaso; Archer

Trapp; Traore, Chergui, Coppola, Otavio; Lopez, Lees Melou; Kebbal, Pagis, Simon; Sissoko

Auxerre's league-worst defensive record is concerning, but conceding just five goals across four home matches suggests that Saturday's assignment may be less straightforward than the table implies.

Paris have struggled to replicate their home performances on the road, and Sinayoko's potential absence could leave Rosenior's men settling for a point.

#2141. Martin O'Neill reveals Celtic masterplan behind game-changing subs

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill claimed his game-changing triple substitution was always part of the plan after the switches rescued his side’s Europa League hopes.

Subs Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran were the heroes as the Hoops came from behind to beat Besiktas 3-2 and get off the mark in the tournament at the fourth time of asking.

The Hoops struggled to get into the Besiktas penalty box before Duran, Osmand and Colby Donovan came on just after the hour mark.

James Forrest had forced the only save for the visiting goalkeeper before then and Celtic trailed 1-0 after Jordan Lotomba conceded a penalty on his first start.

But Osmand fired home with his first touch and set up Duran for the first of the Colombian’s two goals as Celtic emerged victorious in a thrilling finale.

Kasper Hogh and Sebastian Tounekti had offered little threat or safe possession of the ball and the difference in performance after the triple change was striking.

“It was designed to do exactly what it did,” O’Neill said of his selection choices.

“We have been playing Sunday, Thursday, Sunday, Thursday, Wednesday, whatever day it happens to be. We have played, I don’t know, nine games in 23 or 24 days.

“Some players needed a little breather and you can get re-energised from coming on the field.

“So I’m going to say that this was exactly our plan and those players who came on were going to come on at some stage or another in the game.”

The crowd played their part in a memorable final half-an-hour as Celtic secured a fourth win in 11 matches.

Fans had reacted angrily after a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk on Sunday, but the players got them back on their side with their reaction to going behind and when Duran netted seconds after Besiktas equalised in the 86th minute.

“They were a credit to the football club and you can’t get a bigger accolade than that,” O’Neill said. “They were really, really terrific.

“We could have caved in. We were doing fine then the penalty goes in, but we came roaring back. Substitutes made a big, big difference, got a lot of pace up front, but I was just delighted with the whole team.

“It might just give us a platform to charge on. It’s not going to be easy, but at least we can park the European events for a few weeks’ time, but this definitely gives us a chance.”

#2140. Puzzling Liverpool are not ready for the title, why Cole Palmer may have to leave Chelsea and Lisandro Martinez should have lost his spot long ago: IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend

Published: 07:09 EDT, 2 November 2026 | Updated: 12:20 EDT, 2 November 2026

In terms of points gathered, the Premier League title winner this season will be either Arsenal or Manchester City.

It's a two-horse race in which one of the horses has a bullet with its name on it sitting somewhere in a locked cabinet at Premier League headquarters.

We can presume, then, that Arsenal will win the title for the second season running.

Some are entertaining the idea that Brighton can have a go on our behalf. They have beaten Arsenal already at the Amex Stadium and now, after another brilliantly brave display at the Etihad on Saturday, they have beaten City too.

Fabian Hurzeler's team will not win the Premier League, though. Injuries, fluctuations in form and the fact they are playing in Europe will see to that.

Brighton have just played back-to-back games at City – the first in the Carabao Cup last week – and are off to Getafe in the Conference League on Thursday before facing Brentford back in Sussex on Sunday.

Liverpool are not ready to challenge for the Premier League title - and that is OK

It's exciting and it's fun but it's also a schedule that will get them in the end.

As for Liverpool, they are simply not ready. Not yet.

That was apparent before yesterday's home defeat to Arsenal, in which they played well.

Andoni Iraola's team also played nicely at home to City last month but lost that one too.

In fact, Liverpool have lost at home to both their rivals without scoring a goal. They don't score many against anybody, as it happens. Just 11 in the league which is three fewer than Ipswich and only one more than Manchester United.

So, no, Liverpool will not challenge for the title and that should be viewed as perfectly OK on Merseyside.

Liverpool have spent a lot of money since lifting the trophy under Arne Slot in 2025 but some of it has not been spent awfully well and last season was so very bad that they are coming from a long way back under their new manager.

There has been progress. Liverpool have recruited two sound defenders in Jeremy Jacquet and Ronaldo Araujo and are starting to see a return on Alexander Isak and, to a lesser degree, on Florian Wirtz, who has been nowhere near as bad this season as some people seem so keen to claim.

But Liverpool remain a puzzle in the final third. They play with nowhere near the structure and balance of Arsenal or the imagination and pace of City. Yesterday at Anfield was rather typical of how they can be. Possession, promise and power but a lack of calm intelligence and threat just when it really matters.

It may yet come. It is possible to see Iraola's influence. They would appear to have hired the right man to succeed Slot and that is half the battle.

But a third-placed finish, a journey to the last eight of the Champions League and a tilt at a domestic cup would represent progress for Liverpool.

As such – unless City escape their Premier League charges via appeal – this is Arsenal's title already and if that feels rather ho-hum and disappointing, it's for the rest of the competition to ask themselves how it has come to be this way.

Liverpool deserved to get something from the game at Anfield but warrant little sympathy for the manner in which they fell behind.

The home team's problems began when Virgil van Dijk took a goal kick and passed the ball a yard to his right to his goalkeeper Alisson Becker, who proceeded to give it away.

This is a common modern trend but no less confusing for it.

How have we reached a point where so many Premier League clubs seem happier for a goalkeeper to have the ball at his feet than they do an outfield player?

Van Dijk can pass the ball perfectly well. Let him do it!

Brighton are the league's top scorers with 24 and have had 11 different players on target so far.

That's more scorers than half the 20 Premier League clubs have scored goals.

Brighton celebrate a brilliant victory away at Man City - but they won't win the league

Nottingham Forest have to break free from their boom and bust cycle if they are ever to make serious Premier League progress and it feels as though that time is now.

Forest and their owner Evangelos Marinakis are on their fifth manager in the last 14 months. If normal rules apply, Oliver Glasner is in serious trouble after starting the season with just one win in nine games.

But Glasner was the manager Marinakis had wanted for quite some time. He first asked him to join in early 2024 at a time when Nuno Espirito Santo was struggling for results.

So now is the time for the Forest owner to look back at the churn of managers, players and indeed recruitment executives that has characterised his time at the City Ground and realise that something must change.

Glasner was unsparing in his criticism of the Forest players after Saturday's defeat at Brentford. In the same breath, he almost invited Marinakis to sack him.

But Forest's players could be forgiven for being confused and a little demotivated after so much change. Every time they lose back-to-back games, they must expect the manager to be sacked.

So it's time to shift that culture of uncertainty at Forest. Time to behave like a grown-up football club.

Glasner is extremely well paid by Marinakis. His annual salary is north of £10million a season and puts him up near the top of the list.

If Marinakis believes he has a manager of that standing, he should take his hands off the wheel and let him get on with it.

Oliver Glasner invited the sack from Nottingham Forest - but they should stick with him

Michael Carrick will do well to get much more time at Manchester United and there was a certain irony in Lisandro Martinez being the latest player to let him down as his team lost 2-0 at Chelsea.

Martinez – sent off after conceding a ludicrous penalty at Stamford Bridged – moaned publicly last month that United's recruitment hasn't been good enough in recent times.

Had it been any better, a seriously limited and unreliable central defender would have lost his place in the United first team a long time ago.

Carrick knows how this ends but what changes?

United actually played very well in the first half on Saturday and could easily have been two or three goals up by half-time, none of which will be of any comfort to their manager.

We have seen this movie before at Old Trafford.

Carrick will go, United's bunch of semi-serious footballers will raise their levels for a new manager and the club will start telling everyone they have cracked the code – again.

All of which goes to prove what we have known for a long time. Until the quality and indeed the mentality of the players changes at United then nothing else does.

Lisandro Martinez was the latest player to let Michael Carrick down away at Chelsea

Jamie Carragher believes Unai Emery is ready for a step up from Aston Villa to manage a club like United but has upset the Midlands club by saying so.

A Villa statement threatening to sue Carragher for his comments was simply embarrassing.

Carragher's language on the Stick to Football podcast was coarse and he may regret that but it was hard to take issue with his view that Villa sit below United in terms of profile and status.

Villa have made fabulous progress under Emery but part of becoming a really big club is learning how to behave like one.

Cole Palmer now has 50 Premier League goals in 105 games for Chelsea. Only Diego Costa and Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reached that milestone more quickly.

Time will tell, however, whether Chelsea really will provide him with the platform for success his elite level of talent really deserves.

For all that they seem to be moving in the right direction under Xabi Alonso, Saturday's performance against a team waiting to be beaten was still some way below the level a team needs if it is to launch a credible title challenge.

Can Chelsea provide the platform for Cole Palmer that his talent really deserves?

Palmer will be lucky to find his way into Thomas Tuchel's England squad that will be announced on Friday.

His form perhaps warrants it but Tuchel was unimpressed by his withdrawal from the last international gathering and is unlikely to have forgotten.

What, meanwhile, of Trent Alexander-Arnold?

With Reece James and Tino Livramento still injured, the return to fitness of Ben White and Djed Spence has nevertheless given Tuchel some options at right-back for big Nations League games at home to Croatia and away in Spain.

Jarell Quansah can expect to start in Madrid for the game that matters leaving Alexander-Arnold to yet again consider the wisdom of his switch from Liverpool to Real in the summer of 2025.

Alexander-Arnold actually started for Jose Mourinho as Real won 3-0 at Racing yesterday but it was only the fourth time he has done so this season.

At some stage, Alexander-Arnold is going to have to make a decision regarding his future.

Anyone who has seen Tottenham play this season could or should have told you that the improvement on last term was obvious, even when early results were poor.

The London club may well have paid top-heavy prices for new players such as Sandro Tonali and the Manchester City duo of Savio and Omar Marmoush and the value of those deals will become apparent over time.

But Roberto de Zerbi's squad has more depth and balance to it and is benefitting in particular from the improvement in players he inherited from Thomas Frank.

We all remember Antonin Kinsky's Champions League horror show as Spurs collapsed at Atletico Madrid last March but the 23-year-old goalkeeper has been excellent this term.

So, meanwhile, has former England international Conor Gallagher who looked like he had forgotten how to play on arrival last season but was impressive once again in Saturday's win over Crystal Palace, this time as a second-half substitute for Dominic Solanke.

The fuss made about some clubs failing to sell out every single home game is ridiculous given the financial strains currently being placed on families across the country.

Still, it's strange to note pockets of empty blue seats at Coventry matches given how long the club have waited for a top-flight return.

Home games are listed as sold out yet rarely seem to be. Fans say it's because it's too difficult to pass a season ticket on to a friend on days they can't make it.

It's not a good look for Coventry and feels like a problem that needs solving.

There have been regular pockets of empty blue seats at Coventry matches at home this season

Sunderland captain Granit Xhaka called on his players to show courage and play as they train after their defeat at Coventry pinned them to the foot of the table.

But the uncomfortable truth is that nobody in Regis le Bris's team has struggled for form more than the experienced midfielder in recent weeks.

Xhaka was a success story last season as Sunderland stunned the Premier League but needs to find some of that Player of the Year form quickly.

#2139. Arsenal suffer fresh injury blow as Mikel Arteta reveals "some issues" after Slavia Prague win

By Lewis Blain | 05 Nov 2026 07:21

Arsenal have suffered a potential injury setback after Ezri Konsa was forced off during their 2-1 win over Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday evening.

Mikel Arteta confirmed the England defender was substituted because of a fitness issue, having appeared to struggle with his knee during the match.

However, the Gunners have received a timely boost with William Saliba now fit and available again after recovering from a long-term back injury.

Konsa started alongside Gabriel in the heart of Arsenal's defence but was withdrawn shortly after the hour mark following a difficult second half.

The centre-back was spotted feeling his knee during the opening period before continuing after the interval, although he was eventually replaced by Arteta.

The Arsenal manager confirmed the substitution was fitness-related rather than tactical, explaining that the defender had been playing a considerable amount of football recently.

"Obviously he's playing a lot," Arteta said after the match, via the Evening Standard. "He's played so many games in the last few weeks. He had some issues, and we decided to take him off."

Konsa's fitness will now be monitored, particularly with Arsenal continuing to juggle their domestic and European commitments.

There was better news regarding William Saliba, however, with the Frenchman returning to the matchday squad after missing the start of the season with a back injury.

Before the match, Arteta confirmed that the 25-year-old had completed 45 minutes in a behind-closed-doors friendly without any setbacks, and claimed that "he feels ready to go" and "feels really comfortable."

Saliba's return could hardly have come at a better time for the Gunners, particularly with Konsa now carrying a potential injury concern.

The summer signing has hugely impressed alongside Gabriel, but having another established centre-back available means Arteta is not suddenly short of options.

There would be some risk in throwing Saliba straight back into the starting XI against Hull City on Saturday, especially after such a lengthy absence.

However, the upcoming fixture could offer a relatively favourable opportunity to gradually reintegrate the Frenchman, provided Arteta is satisfied with his fitness.

Konsa's situation will need assessing before any decisions are made, but Saliba's availability gives Arsenal some welcome defensive insurance at an important stage of the campaign.

#2138. Enzo Maresca now doubles down on his Gianluigi Donnarumma stance after latest Man City "mistake"

By Lewis Blain | 05 Nov 2026 07:47

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has defended Gianluigi Donnarumma once again following another costly mistake during their 3-2 win over RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday evening.

The Italian goalkeeper was criticised after allowing Ridle Baku's effort to beat him at the near post, adding to a growing list of errors this season.

However, Maresca has shown little indication that he intends to reconsider his first-choice goalkeeper ahead of Saturday's trip to face Nottingham Forest at the City Ground in the Premier League.

Donnarumma came under scrutiny after City's latest Champions League victory, having been unable to prevent Baku from equalising shortly after half-time.

The mistake followed previous errors against Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain, raising questions about the 27-year-old's consistency since arriving at the Etihad Stadium.

However, Maresca insisted that the incident was not a major concern, highlighting the goalkeeper's ability to produce important saves at the other end.

"It's not a concern, but it's a mistake," the City manager told reporters, via the BBC. "He recognises, he knows that it's a mistake. And now, in 48 hours, we have Nottingham Forest away, and we need to be focused on that."

Maresca was also asked whether the upcoming international break could provide an opportunity to reconsider his goalkeeping options, but again defended Donnarumma.

"I'm not thinking about the goalkeeper situation," he said. "We're talking about a mistake, but a few minutes before, he's done a save that any keeper in the world, they're not going to do that save!"

The City boss added that Donnarumma knows his performance was "not good" enough but believes he will improve in the coming weeks.

Donnarumma's recent errors are becoming difficult to ignore, particularly given his struggles with distribution and dealing with crosses into the penalty area.

However, Maresca's options behind the Italian are not particularly convincing, making a change difficult to justify.

City allowed James Trafford to leave during the summer, despite the Englishman's potential, and arguably made their own situation more complicated by not retaining a capable alternative.

Geronimo Rulli remains the back-up, and despite penalty heroics against Brighton & Hove Albion in the Carabao Cup, Maresca has already made clear that Donnarumma is his undisputed first choice.

The Italian's shot-stopping ability is also a major asset, as demonstrated by several outstanding interventions this season.

Despite the mistakes, it is difficult to envisage Maresca dropping Donnarumma anytime soon. The 6 foot 5 shot-stopper needs to improve his consistency, but City may have to persist with him given their current alternatives.

#2137. Martin O'Neill gushes over 'class' Celtic star after European heroics

Camilo Duran earned glowing praise from Martin O’Neill after coming off the bench to fire Celtic to a dramatic Europa League victory over Besiktas.

The Colombian struck twice in a thrilling 3-2 win at Celtic Park as the Hoops finally got off the mark in the competition on their fourth attempt.

Duran was introduced alongside Callum Osmand and Colby Donovan shortly after the hour mark with Celtic trailing 1-0 and struggling to seriously threaten the visitors. The changes transformed the contest.

Osmand equalised with his first touch just 49 seconds after entering the action before setting up Duran to put Celtic ahead. Besiktas hit back to make it 2-2, but Duran struck again late on to complete his double and seal a huge European victory.

O’Neill was delighted with the impact of the forward and revealed he had always intended to introduce him from the bench. “Duran has been fabulous for us all season and got his two goals,” O’Neill said.

“He has played a lot of games and looked a bit tired in the last couple. But he’s a class player, and he was always going to come on.

“I’m delighted with the performance. It was fantastic.”

The victory brought back memories of O’Neill’s first spell in charge of Celtic as a raucous home crowd roared their side to victory. “That was a special European night,” he said. “It reminded me of the olden days.

“The subs re-energised us and played a big part in the win.”

Martin O'Neill reveals Celtic masterplan behind game-changing subs

Martin O'Neill fires 'a lot more' Celtic demand at £3.5m signing

The telling Michael Nicholson quip that reveals Celtic's transfer strategy

O’Neill was particularly pleased with the character his players showed after falling behind and then being pegged back at 2-2 late in the game. “I told the players afterwards that they are a credit to the club,” he added.

“You can’t get a bigger accolade than that, but we put our heart and soul into the game. We played really good stuff, particularly in the second half.

"At 2-2, it looked like we would drop two points but we came roaring back to win the game. There was so much spirit and desire to get the three points. The character shone through big time.

"The winners came to the fore, as did the new boys.”

Duran also earned praise from fellow substitute Osmand following his match-winning display. “Camilo did amazing; he’s such a poacher,” He said. “Credit to him.

“The team dug in, stayed strong and we got our rewards. I was so happy to come on, score a goal and get the win.”

The victory gave Celtic renewed hope of progressing in the Europa League ahead of their meeting with Portuguese second-tier side Torreense on November 26. O’Neill said: “We rose to the occasion and we have given ourselves a chance.

“We are off the mark now. We have points on the board, and we can park it for a few weeks now. There is still a thought about qualifying, but that is a long way off.

“Hopefully it gives us a platform to charge on, but it’s not going to be easy.”

#2136. Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#2135. Nottingham Forest vs Manchester City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 08:00, Last updated: 06 Nov 2026 17:45

Second from bottom faces second from top in the Premier League on Saturday evening, as Nottingham Forest welcome Manchester City to the City Ground.

The two teams played out a 2-2 draw in their last meeting at the Etihad Stadium in March, with Elliot Anderson scoring a late equaliser for Forest before completing his big-money move to City in the summer.

Man City strengthened their hopes of securing automatic qualification for the Champions League last 16 with a 3-2 away victory over RB Leipzig on Wednesday, climbing into seventh place in the 36-team League Phase table at the halfway stage.

Manager Enzo Maresca has admitted that his team “struggled” in moments against Leipzig, but the German club’s nemesis Erling Haaland – wearing the captain’s armband – was on hand to slide home a 78th-minute match-winner for City and his 13th goal in just nine games against Die Roten Bullen.

The Citizens were made to work for their victory over Leipzig having previously suffered back-to-back Premier League defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton & Hove Albion, results that forced them to surrender top spot in the table to champions Arsenal.

City’s 24-game scoring streak in the Premier League was halted by a high-flying Seagulls side who battled to a narrow 1-0 victory at the Etihad last weekend, despite Maresca’s men registering 21 shots worth 1.92 expected goals (xG) and over 60% possession.

Not since February/March 2016 under Manuel Pellegrini have Man City lost three PL games in a row, and they head to the City Ground this weekend having won two of their previous four league visits (D1 L1) since Forest’s return to the top flight in 2022, most recently winning 2-1 in December last year.

Oliver Glasner has not made the desired impact as Nottingham Forest head coach, with his team winning only one of their opening nine Premier League games (D3 L5) and accumulating just a single point from their last 15 available, leaving them down in 19th place in the table.

Scoring goals has been the key issue for the Tricky Trees, who are the Premier League’s joint-lowest scorers (six) and have drawn a blank in five of their nine matches, despite registering the second-most shots per game in the division (16.9), only behind Manchester United (18.6).

A further 15 shots and just one on target in the 78th minute was recorded in last weekend’s 2-0 defeat at Brentford - another frustrating result that sparked a passionate post-match rant from Glasner, demanding his players to 'either buy in to changes or leave' to ensure that last season’s “s*** situation” does not repeat itself.

Forest’s hierarchy have reportedly welcomed Glasner’s strong words, but the real test is whether his misfiring squad will finally respond on the pitch. The Tricky Trees remains winless and goalless in five home fixtures this season, losing their last two to Coventry and Arsenal by a 1-0 scoreline.

Glasner now faces a daunting task against Man City, having lost four of his previous five league meetings with them (D1) during his time as Crystal Palace boss, conceding at least three goals in each defeat. However, Forest can draw confidence from their 1-0 home victory over City just two seasons ago, thanks to a late Callum Hudson-Odoi strike.

Nottingham Forest form (all competitions):

Nottingham Forest duo Nicolo Savona (knee) and Igor Jesus (calf) have both trained this week, but Saturday's game will come too soon for the former, while Nicolas Dominguez (muscle) is ruled out for around eight weeks.

Former Man City youngster Liam Delap has failed to score in his last five starts for Forest and is at risk of losing his centre-forward spot to Chris Wood, who is still waiting to start hist first league game of the season.

James McAtee – another ex-City player – has made a notable impression in a deeper midfield role where he is expected to continue, while Daniel Munoz – who has been managing a minor foot issue – and Ousmane Diomande will both be pushing for recalls in defence.

As for Man City, Maresca is not expected to make wholesale changes, but captain Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol are strong contenders to earn a recall in defence at the expense of Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly, who has been left out of the England squad due to fitness-related reasons.

Enzo Fernandez, who scored his first UCL goal for City in midweek, is the most likely midfielder to play alongside Anderson, though Ayyoub Bouaddi and Mateo Kovacic are two central options pushing to replace the Argentine.

Haaland – without a goal in his last four appearances against Forest – will lead the line once again and could be supported in attack by Iliman Ndiaye, Rayan Cherki and Jeremy Doku, the latter of whom began as a substitute against Leipzig.

Nottingham Forest possible starting lineup:

Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams; Ndoye, Gibbs-White; Delap

Manchester City possible starting lineup:

Donnarumma; Nunes, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

Forest’s misfiring frontline is a growing concern for Glasner, but the hosts should take encouragement from Man City’s porous defence that has conceded 14 goals in their last seven games in all competitions.

A closely-contested battle could be in store this weekend, but we expect the Citizens to possess the clinical edge required to claim maximum points.
